results.drift: DRIFT on two counts. (1) Capitalisation: every occurrence in every source is lower-case and mid-sentence — "…are/is at least one trillion times more likely…". A case-sensitive search for "At least one trillion" or "At least 1 trillion" across the whole artifact bank returns ZERO hits; the phrase never begins a sentence and never stands alone. (2) Truncation that drops the qualifier: the source phrase is never a bare magnitude. It is always the first half of a two-proposition conditional — e.g. "The DNA profile is at least one trillion times more likely if it originated from Tyler Robinson as a major component and three unrelated unknown individuals than if it originated from four unrelated unknown individuals." Cutting at "trillion" removes "times more likely", the conditioning hypothesis, and the alternative hypothesis, converting a likelihood RATIO between two stated propositions into an unanchored number. This is the exact failure QUEUE.md hazard 14 was written about (the false "Day 4 delivered the trillion figures with none of the qualifications" finding) — the qualifications are present in the record, eight verbatim readings of Paragraph D in full conditional form. Also note the final-argument text mixes renderings within one speech: "at least 1 trillion" (numeral) and "at least one trillion" (word) both appear.
